author: evanboyle
body:
The goal of this PR is to improve GenSX react integration by having a story for defining state in the server, and then streaming that state over the wire, and consuming it via a well typed react hook. 

This PR adds: 

- gensx primitives for state: `workflowState` `componentState` `StatefulComponent` (and tests!)
- `@gensx/react` package for the new react hooks
- blog-writer-react example that shows the hole experience e2e
- various updates and bug fixes to the dev server to make it work well inside of a next.js project

I still have a few TODOs I'm cleaning up, but it is ready enough to have folks start to take a look. 

One thing we should discuss is the name for "State", and if we want to call it something else like "Status". 

The `state-design.md` file is the document that I used with cursor as I was designing this. I will leave it for now so that folks can read it for an overview, but I will remove it before merging.

### Link to issue number:
<!-- Use Closes/Fixes/Resolves #xxx to link this PR to the issue it is responding to. -->
Fixes #18231

### Summary of the issue:

Previously, JABTextInfo's _getParagraphOffsets used its own _getLineOffsets to obtain paragraph offsets, which resulted in only the line under the mouse being reported in the paragraph mouse text unit.

### Description of user facing changes:

Now report the paragraph under the mouse.

### Description of developer facing changes:

JABTextInfo obtains the correct offset for the paragraph.

### Description of development approach:

* The `_getStoryText` method has been added to `JABTextInfo` so that `OffsetsTextInfo._getLineOffsets` can work.
* `JABTextInfo._getParagraphOffsets` now uses the superclass `_getLineOffsets` to calculate offsets based on text content.

### Testing strategy:

This PR only affects cases where the mouse text unit is a paragraph.

Run [TextComponentDemo.java](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/uiswing/examples/components/TextComponentDemoProject/src/components/TextComponentDemo.java) to test.

Manual testing:

1. Report the entire paragraph when the mouse is over a multi-line paragraph.
2. Enter some text on the last line, and report the text just entered when the mouse is on the last line.
3. When the last line is empty, the mouse reports the contents of the penultimate line and its paragraph on the last line. Similar to #9376, no regression was introduced.

author: differencesm
body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code documentation](http://docs.anthropic.com/s/claude-code-github-actions).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: snorrees
body: # Custom field actions To incorporate [Agent Actions](https://www.sanity.io/docs/agent-actions?utm_source=github.com&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=ai-assist&utm_content=) or other custom actions into the AI Assist document and field action menus, use `fieldActions` plugin config: ```ts assist({ title: 'Custom actions', useFieldActions: (props: AssistFieldActionProps) => { return useMemo(() => [ defineAssistFieldAction({ title: 'Do something', icon: ActionIcon, onAction: async () => { // perform an (async) action // errors will be caught and displayed in a toast // until the action completes or fails, AI Assist "presence" will show up on the top of the document }, })], []) } }) ``` Read the new README section for details: https://github.com/sanity-io/assist/tree/custom-actions/plugin#custom-field-actions ### Testing The test studio now has a small handful of custom actions configured. Visit: https://ai-assist-test.sanity.studio/structure/mockArticle Try the document action "Populate document about": ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2afcd74b-31e8-48e7-9361-ceffeb5be9b2) It is a slow action that first: * prompts for an outline * the prompts for more content * the finally runs generate The purple Assist indicator should be showing for the duration of the action (as long as you dont navigate away – its client side orchestration. If you want to be able to reload you would have to call a function that does it all). Try the field actions: ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4c8e0a9e-61cc-4e27-8d89-c69afcf12641) * "Fill field" uses "all the props" to create a field-contextual generate action that will contextually generate based on what is already in the document. * "Throws" will run a throwing sync action. The error is logged and a toast is displayed. * "Async Throws" will run a throwing async action. The action is awaited, the error is logged and a toast is displayed. * Log user input logs the returned value from the user input dialog it displays. Feel free to play with the api locally as you see fit. ### Image for readme ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c613f692-4983-4acc-a8c2-8fb60294682a)

author: fedepaol
body:
We add a l2vni type to offer a way to extend a l2 domain via a vxlan
overlay.

As opposed to l3vni veths which land directly in the vrf routing space
corresponding to the ip domain of a l3 VNI, here we enslave the veth leg
inside the PE router to the linux bridge which extends the l2 domain,
effectively adding a way to plug the domain.

Additionally, we expose a knob to either plug the host part of the veth
to an existing bridge, or to automatically create one, which is
particularly convenient in case we want to use the macvlan CNI to add a
pod to the l2 domain.

author: okom1
body:
## Changes

**Added**

Weapons:
- [119] Rocket Hog Weapon (Vehicle weapon)
- [120] Wasp Weapon (Vehicle weapon)
- [121] Rocket Hog Weapon + Backdraft Cindershot (Vehicle weapon)
- [122] Rocket Hog Weapon + Rapidfire Pulse Carbine (Vehicle weapon)
- [123] Rocket Hog Weapon + Ravager Rebound (Vehicle weapon)
- [124] Rocket Hog Weapon + Unbound Plasma Pistol (Vehicle weapon)
- [125] Wasp Weapon + Scatterbound Heatwave (Vehicle weapon)

Vehicles:
- [13] Extermination Gungoose (REQ 4)
- [14] Fusion Rocket Hog (REQ 7)
- [15] Plasma Warthog (REQ 6)
- [16] Phantom Wasp (REQ 8)
- [17] Banishing Wasp (REQ 9)

**Adjusted:**

Vehicles:
- [7] Scorpion
    - REQ Tier: 8 -> **9**

## Custom vehicle additions

Following a scripting discovery by Discord user [coke_cane](https://discord.com/channels/220766496635224065/952263098734084136/1378028058136674305), the vehicle weapon on the Rocket Hog and Wasp were able to be extracted, and combined with legendary weapon configurations to produce weapon types that were usable by vehicles. Normally vehicles don't accept using regular weapons, but if the base weapon is one native to the vehicle, they seem to work.

After the discovery, we went through all possible combinations with the two base vehicle weapons available to us and created five brand new vehicle variants, which are all upgrades to their normal vehicle versions.

### Extermination Gungoose

A Mongoose shooting three Scatterbound Heatwave shots in a single shotgun-like burst. Landing the majority of these shots is enough to instantly kill a Ghost; landing the majority of the shots is the difficult part, but the vehicle allows for shooting the Heatwave shots in any direction regardless where the vehicle is facing. The cooldown between each shot is 3.3 seconds which is the balancing factor of the vehicle, and brings it to REQ tier 4.

### Fusion Rocket Hog

A Rocket Hog shooting Backdraft Cindershot projectiles from the turret, with Pulse Carbine-like shot-tracking within red-reticle range. This is the ultimate anti-air vehicle in our sandbox, as the Cindershot projectiles have a unique ability by inheriting a very strong tracking to enemy targets while in red-reticle range.

This vehicle is not only much stronger at damaging vehicles due to the Hardlight damage type, but it's also more consistent at landing the shots compared to the default Rocket Hog as the shots track so aggressively, and also split into multiple projectiles upon explosion. While the vehicle health remains the same, this extreme offensive ability towards even the higher-end of vehicles lands this vehicle variant at REQ tier 7.

### Plasma Warthog

A Warthog shooting Unbound Plasma Pistol shots from the chaingun turret at an alarming rate with no cooldown. The plasma damage is great at melting enemy player shields, but is also faster at destroying vehicles than the normal Warthog turret.

The balancing factor of this variant is the projectile speed of the Plasma Pistol shots, which travel at 50 m/s compared to the hitscan shots of the default turret. This slow travel time makes it difficult to hit moving targets, but the slight bullet magnetism within red reticle range is still helping guide those shots. With these caveats in mind this vehicle lands at REQ tier 6.

### Phantom Wasp

A Wasp shooting Rapidfire Pulse Carbine shots from the chaingun, and retaining the default rockets on the secondary weapon. A stationary aerial vehicle that shoots fast-moving plasma projectiles at around 100 m/s and still has access to the deadly double rocket of the Wasp is one to fear during the late game of Warzone.

While the Pulse Carbine primary weapon may not appeal to everyone at first glance, its power is deadly if the pilot is accurate enough to land even a few of them on unsuspecting infantry. This config doesn't suffer from the bloom of the default Wasp's chaingun either, so as long as you're within medium range of your target and your shots are landing on them, they won't be standing for long.

This is only still a slight upgrade from the normal Wasp, as its health stays the same. We've initially placed the Phantom Wasp at REQ tier 8.

### Banishing Wasp

A Wasp shooting Rebound Ravager shots at a constant and unending rate at the cost of losing the secondary rocket firing ability. Shooting approximately 2.5 bouncing Rebound Ravager shots every second, this aerial gunship is intended for mass damage over a group of enemies, or against vehicles.

While the vehicle has a massive damage output potential if aimed and controlled carefully, it still benefits from no health or movement buffs, leading to it being a glass cannon of mass destruction. Due to its unmatched and unending damage output potential and nimble maneuvering ablities in the sky, the Banishing Wasp becomes available at REQ tier 9.

## Scorpion tier adjustment

Following feedback from player Precellence, and internal observations about the high impact of the Scorpion at REQ tier 8, we've moved it up a tier to REQ 9. In year 5 of Halo Infinite the Scorpion still remains an overpowered vehicle against any other weapon in the default sandbox. We will continue to monitor how powerful the Scorpion stays in Warzone, and have plans to reduce its health if it's still overpowering the rest of the sandbox.

body:
I've implemented a FastAPI server for EchoRead with a comprehensive set of mock API endpoints as outlined in the project's README.md.

Key accomplishments:
- **FastAPI App Setup:** Initialized the FastAPI application in `api_server/main.py`.
- **Pydantic Models:** Created Pydantic models in `api_server/models.py` to define data structures for users, books, audios, and playback, serving as a mock database.
- **Requirements:** Generated a `requirements.txt` for dependencies (FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic, etc.).
- **Authentication Router (`routers/auth.py`):**
    - `POST /auth/google`: Mock Google OAuth2 token exchange for a JWT.
    - `POST /auth/logout`: Mock JWT invalidation.
- **User Router (`routers/users.py`):**
    - `GET /users/me`: Mock retrieval of authenticated user profile, using a mock JWT.
- **Books Router (`routers/books.py`):**
    - `POST /books/upload`: Mock EPUB file upload, initiating conceptual TTS processing.
    - `GET /books`: List your books.
    - `GET /books/{book_id}`: Get detailed book information.
    - `DELETE /books/{book_id}`: Mock book deletion.
    - `GET /books/{book_id}/status`: Mock TTS generation progress.
    - `GET /books/{book_id}/audios`: List mock chapter audios.
    - `GET /books/{book_id}/audios/{audio_id}`: Return mock MP3 audio data.
- **Playback Router (`routers/plays.py`):**
    - `POST /plays`: Mock saving last playback position.
    - `GET /plays/{book_id}`: Mock retrieving last playback position.
- **Router Integration:** All routers included in `main.py`.
- **Mocking Strategy:** Utilized in-memory Python dictionaries for data persistence and mock functions for processes like TTS.

The implementation currently uses relative imports and a `requirements.txt` file.

**Further User Requirements (Not Yet Implemented):** You have requested the following changes for future development:
- Use absolute imports throughout the `api_server`.
- Manage package dependencies using Poetry instead of `requirements.txt`.
- Implement database interactions using SQLAlchemy with a PostgreSQL database.
- Database connection details to be determined by a `dev.env` file.

These changes represent a significant refactoring and were not part of the initial plan. The current code provides a functional mock API server based on the original understanding. The README update with usage examples for the current API was the next planned step but is deferred due to this being the final turn.

body:
<!--
Note: This template is a reminder of our Engineering Expectations and Definition of Done. Remove sections that don't apply to your changes.

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1199333091098016/task/1210505420118693?focus=true
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description

Apply a workaround for the iOS 18.4 and 18.5 simulator linking issue.

For convenience, I've attached a copy of the script at the bottom of the description.

### Testing Steps
<!-- Assume the reviewer is unfamiliar with this part of the app -->
1. Check that the simulator builds and runs for 18.3 (or 18.3.1)
2. Now do a clean build and try the same for 18.4
3. Finally, do another clean build and test 18.5 

### Impact and Risks
<!-- 
What's the impact on users if something goes wrong?

High: Could affect user privacy, lose user data, break core functionality
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows
Low: Minor visual changes, small bug fixes, improvement to existing features
None: Internal tooling, documentation
-->

#### What could go wrong?
<!-- Describe specific scenarios and how you've addressed them -->

In theory this change is safe since it only affects the simulator, and only two versions of iOS. Worst case the build will fail, but that's already the case. :)

### Quality Considerations
<!-- 
Focus on what matters for your changes:
- What edge cases exist?
- How does this affect performance?
- What monitoring have you added?
- What documentation needs updating?
- How does this impact privacy/security?
-->

### Notes to Reviewer
<!-- Anything specific you want reviewers to focus on -->

---

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
###############################################################################
#
# Several simulator runtimes (18.4, 18.5, 26.0) ship without the Swift
# overlay libswiftWebKit.dylib. This script copies the missing dylib from the
# runtime into $BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR so the app can launch under those sims.
# Delete the script once Apple ships corrected runtimes.
###############################################################################
set -euo pipefail

readonly DYLIB_NAME="libswiftWebKit.dylib"

###############################################################################
# 1. Guard – run only for *iphonesimulator* builds
###############################################################################

if [[ "${PLATFORM_NAME:-}" != "iphonesimulator" ]]; then
    echo "ℹ️  Skipping $DYLIB_NAME workaround – PLATFORM_NAME='${PLATFORM_NAME:-unset}'"
    exit 0
fi

###############################################################################
# 2. Validate TARGET_DEVICE_OS_VERSION is available
###############################################################################

if [[ -z "${TARGET_DEVICE_OS_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
    echo "❌ TARGET_DEVICE_OS_VERSION environment variable is not set" >&2
    exit 1
fi

echo "ℹ️  Target device OS version: $TARGET_DEVICE_OS_VERSION"

###############################################################################
# 3. Configuration for supported versions (Bash 3.x compatible)
###############################################################################

get_build_id_for_version() {
    case "$1" in
        18.4*) echo "22E238" ;;
        18.5*) echo "22F77" ;;
        *) return 1 ;;
    esac
}

get_runtime_dylib_path() {
    local version="$1"
    local build_id
    
    build_id="$(get_build_id_for_version "$version")" || return 1
    
    echo "/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Volumes/iOS_${build_id}/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Profiles/Runtimes/iOS ${version}.simruntime/Contents/Resources/RuntimeRoot/System/Cryptexes/OS/usr/lib/swift/$DYLIB_NAME"
}

###############################################################################
# 4. Check if workaround is needed and find the dylib
###############################################################################

find_matching_runtime() {
    local target_version="$1"
    local runtime_path
    
    runtime_path="$(get_runtime_dylib_path "$target_version")" || {
        return 1
    }
    
    if [[ -f "$runtime_path" ]]; then
        echo "$runtime_path"
        return 0
    else
        echo "⚠️  Runtime dylib not found at: $runtime_path" >&2
        echo "⚠️  Make sure iOS ${target_version%.*} simulator runtime is installed" >&2
        return 1
    fi
}

RUNTIME_DYLIB="$(find_matching_runtime "$TARGET_DEVICE_OS_VERSION")" || {
    echo "✅ Runtime iOS $TARGET_DEVICE_OS_VERSION doesn't require $DYLIB_NAME workaround"
    exit 0
}

###############################################################################
# 5. Validate environment and paths
###############################################################################

if [[ -z "${BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR:-}" ]]; then
    echo "❌ BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR environment variable is not set" >&2
    exit 1
fi

if [[ ! -d "$BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR" ]]; then
    echo "❌ Build products directory does not exist: $BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR" >&2
    exit 1
fi

###############################################################################
# 6. Copy the overlay into the build products directory
###############################################################################

DESTINATION="$BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR/$DYLIB_NAME"

# Skip if files are identical
if [[ -f "$DESTINATION" ]] && cmp -s "$RUNTIME_DYLIB" "$DESTINATION"; then
    echo "ℹ️  $DYLIB_NAME already exists and is identical"
    exit 0
fi

echo "🏗️  Copying $RUNTIME_DYLIB → $DESTINATION"

if /bin/cp -f "$RUNTIME_DYLIB" "$DESTINATION" && /bin/chmod 644 "$DESTINATION"; then
    echo "✅ Successfully applied $DYLIB_NAME workaround for iOS $TARGET_DEVICE_OS_VERSION"
else
    echo "❌ Failed to copy $DYLIB_NAME" >&2
    exit 1
fi
```

body:
#### 3c907c552d9c986d0149653bb629cfcdaec5ac3f 
document should not be null after navigation with site isolation enabled
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=294228
rdar://152872994

Reviewed by Charlie Wolfe.

https://commits.webkit.org/292437@main introduced a case where we take the WindowProxy
from one page to another when navigating the main frame from one domain to another.
If the WindowProxy that we are taking had its JSWindowProxy initialized by an iframe
on the previous page accessing its parent's properties, then JSDOMWindowBase::initStaticGlobals
has already been called to initialize document to null, but ScriptController::initScriptForWindowProxy
won't call JSDOMWindowBase::updateDocument to set document to the document instead of null
because WindowProxy::jsWindowProxy will find an already existing JSWindowProxy initialized
where WindowProxy::createJSWindowProxyWithInitializedScript has skipped the call to
initScriptForWindowProxy because the Frame was a RemoteFrame when it was initialized.

To fix this issue, we add another call to didBecomeCurrentDocumentInFrame after swapping
from a RemoteFrame to a LocalFrame.  That will call updateDocument as well as do
possibly other initialization needed.

I also restore an assertion that was removed in 292437@main, but I added a condition to
make it pass when taking a WindowProxy from one page to another.

This fixes one of the issues I found in rdar://152460976 but not the initial one, so
that still needs more investigation.

body:
This pull request introduces high-level APIs for permanent deletion of entries from the reMarkable cloud/device sync, along with comprehensive tests and documentation. The main additions are the new `purge` and `bulkPurge` methods, which allow for permanent deletion of single or multiple entries, respectively.

### New Permanent Deletion APIs

* Added the `purge` method to the `Remarkable` class, allowing permanent deletion of a single entry by hash. Returns a boolean indicating success.
* Added the `bulkPurge` method to the `Remarkable` class, enabling permanent deletion of multiple entries at once. Returns a dictionary mapping each hash to a boolean indicating whether it was successfully purged. Handles edge cases like empty or duplicate hashes.

### Tests

* Added tests for `purge` and `bulkPurge` in `src/index.spec.ts`, covering successful purges, failures, no-op scenarios, duplicate hashes, and request flow matching the desktop app. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-18466f9d870e2151722b884f1cb0df6c1530517bde9468ec2a5abbbb8f655210R937-R978) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-18466f9d870e2151722b884f1cb0df6c1530517bde9468ec2a5abbbb8f655210R1094-R1236)

body:
## Fixes grok-3-mini (and variants) HTTP response error with stop tokens

While using another project that includes LiteLLM as a dependency, I noticed I was getting an HTTP 400 error when using `grok-3-mini`. See here:

```
BadRequestError: XaiException - Error code: 400 - {'code': 'Client specified an invalid argument', 'error': 'Argument not supported on this model: stop'}
```

The issue was raised here [All-Hands-AI/OpenHands#8988](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/8988). It turns out, however, that the underlying cause of the problem came back to LiteLLM, so I thought I'd make a quick fix for it. The issue here is that, for some reason, `grok-3-mini` and variant models do not accept the `stop` argument. To be clear, it is only those models, as `grok-3` by itself does. I have no idea why that might be, nor why it started happening all of a sudden, but I suspect it is something internal with xAI. In any case, I added a check in the XAI config class to only add 'stop' as a parameter if it is not a `grok-3-mini` model. This way, the HTTP 400 error no longer results, just an exception from litellm about an unsupported model argument (rightly so), or it being silently dropped before making the request if `drop_params` is true. I also added some additional model definitions for xAI models in the models_price_and_context_window.json since `grok-3-mini` is out of beta now.

Fixes [All-Hands-AI/OpenHands#8988](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/8988).

body:
This feature introduces a Node.js script to automatically discover TYPO3 Fluid templates and make them easily accessible in Storybook.

Key changes:

- Added `scripts/discover-fluid-templates.js`:
  - Scans specified TYPO3 extension directories for .html files in Resources/Private/{Templates,Partials,Layouts}.
  - Generates a JSON file mapping unique aliases (e.g., MyExt_Templates_Page_Default) to their full EXT:paths.
  - Supports CLI arguments for specifying extension paths (`--extensions`) and the output JSON file path (`--output`).
  - Includes error handling for invalid paths and file operations.
  - Uses `minimist` for argument parsing.

- Updated `README.md`:
  - Added a new section "Automated Fluid Template Discovery".
  - Documented the purpose, installation (mentioning `minimist`), and usage of the `discover-fluid-templates.js` script with examples.
  - Described the JSON output format.
  - Added a detailed example of how to integrate the generated JSON file into a Storybook story to create a dynamic template selector using `argTypes.select`.

This enhancement streamlines the process of working with multiple Fluid templates in Storybook by reducing manual path configuration.

## Description

This pull request implements dynamic tab management in the dashboard interface, enhancing file navigation and content visualization.

__Key Changes:__

1. __Tab Management System (`frontend/src/hooks/use-tabs.ts`):__

   - Added tab persistence across page refreshes

1. Open multiple files from the sidebar to create tabs

2. Verify tab operations:

   - Switch between tabs
   - Close tabs (click X or middle-click)
   - Drag and drop to reorder tabs
   - Check overflow menu for many tabs

3. Verify persistence:

   - Refresh page - tabs should remain
   - Close all tabs - new tabs should work

4. Test keyboard shortcuts:

   - Ctrl+Tab to cycle tabs
   - Ctrl+W to close current tab
   - Ctrl+1-9 to switch to specific tabs

## Additional Notes

This implementation focuses on providing a robust and user-friendly tab interface similar to modern IDEs, with proper state management and performance optimizations. All changes follow TypeScript strict mode and maintain proper type safety.

This pull request makes changes to the `destinations.component.html` file in the PlanGo frontend application to enhance user interaction and improve the layout of destination details. author: apradhana
body:
- This PR adds `example_rigid_force.py` from Warp to Newton to test the USD Renderer. This is to make sure that the original functionality of the USD Renderer stays intact.
- This PR takes out the renderer functionality used in `sim_usd` that creates a time-samples USD file from a simulation and moves it to `render.py`. This is achieved through adding a new member function called `render_update_stage` which requires a `source_stage` to be updated. This is an example on how this functionality is used:
```python
    def __init__(self, input_path, output_path, input_path):
        ...
        self.renderer = newton.utils.SimRendererUsd(
            self.model,
            stage=output_path,
            source_stage=input_path,
            path_body_relative_transform=self.path_body_relative_transform,
            path_body_map=self.path_body_map,
            builder_results=self.builder_results,
        )

    def render(self):
        with wp.ScopedTimer("render", dict=self.profiler):
            self.renderer.begin_frame(self.sim_time)
            self.renderer.render_update_stage(self.state_0)
            self.renderer.end_frame()
```

This is how `example_rigid_force` looks like:

author: howardjohn
body:
This PR introduces the ability to use a custom pool key with the legacy Client.

https://github.com/hyperium/hyper-util/pull/16 added generic support to `Pool` itself long ago, but it was never fully finished to allow a custom key in `Client`.

To support backwards compatibility, a default PoolKey is assigned to the generic parameter which seems reasonably backwards compatible(?)

When providing a custom pool key, the user is required to also pass a constructor that generates the pool key from the `http::request::Parts`. 

~I had also considered making a user pass in the PoolKey as part of the `request()` call, but I think this is a worse experience generally and harder to be backwards compatible. If a user did want to do a per-request key they can always set an extension in `Parts` so this approach is equally flexible.~ Edit: actually in my POC I realized this was not quite right. With this change, the user can pool based on anything... but then they cannot actually get utilize the extra info in the pool key during the Connector. I am still exploring some possibilities there.
